name: Alpine dusk
_note: The Phase 2 palette. Endpoints unchanged so the default scene is the one the lighting keyframes were tuned against; only the mid stop is new.

name: Glacier
_note: Pale cyan distance falling to a deep meltwater teal — the coldest and highest-key of the set.

name: Sandstone mesa
_note: Warm ochre through burnt sienna. The counterweight to Alpine dusk.

name: Volcanic ash
_note: Near-neutral, but warm-shifted rather than grey so it doesn't collide with Ink wash. Its tint is deliberately the quietest of the eight for the same reason.

name: Ink wash
_note: Deliberately zero-chroma, and its tint is too. A tint with no hue of its own cannot tint anything — it very slightly drains the interface's own colour instead, which is the honest outcome for a palette whose identity is having none, and makes this the control case when checking that the other seven tints are doing something.

name: Desert
_note: Phase 7's demonstrator for Layers mode: rocky mesa brown behind, dune yellow through the middle, sand off-white in front. The one theme whose ramp runs dark-to-pale rather than pale-to-dark, because the band it is naming (foreground sand) is the pale one — see CONTEXT.md section 6d for what that means in continuous mode.
